paper: Exact Compositional Transfer of Bounded Linear Recovery

claims.statement: Minimum-support lifts over the complete outer functional dual give the exact finite rank-stratified nonconfinement cost, and confinement through a helper radius holds exactly below that cost.
claims.objects: Represented inner code, target/helper split, and complete outer functional dual.
claims.hypotheses: Finite fields; nonzero helper-recoverable target; at least two outer blocks and surjective distinguished projection.
claims.conclusion: Minimum-support lifts over the complete outer functional dual give the exact finite rank-stratified nonconfinement cost, and confinement through a helper radius holds exactly below that cost.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: Minimum-weight normalized recovery equations of an MDS code span its dual code.
claims.objects: Normalized minimum-weight equations and the dual of an MDS code.
claims.hypotheses: An [n,k] MDS code with nontrivial dual and a specified coordinate.
claims.conclusion: Minimum-weight normalized recovery equations of an MDS code span its dual code.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: The restricted helper map gives the stated exact sequence for the associated nested code pair.
claims.objects: Kernel K_P, preimage D_P, and intersection W_P of the target and helper generator maps.
claims.hypotheses: Linear target and helper maps into a common vector space; the Lean statement needs neither finite field nor finite coordinates.
claims.conclusion: The restricted helper map gives the stated exact sequence for the associated nested code pair.
claims.cautions: Four source terminals establish the linear exact-sequence components; the quotient identification uses the first isomorphism theorem in the prose. No distance, support optimization, or concatenation theorem is formalized.

claims.statement: The associated nested pair is literally the shortening-puncturing pair of the inner dual on the helper coordinates; its dual pair is the shortening-puncturing pair of the inner code, and both are independent of the chosen generator-row basis.
claims.objects: Associated helper pair and duals inside the helper-coordinate space.
claims.hypotheses: A linear code with a full-row-rank generator and a disjoint target/helper split.
claims.conclusion: The associated nested pair is literally the shortening-puncturing pair of the inner dual on the helper coordinates; its dual pair is the shortening-puncturing pair of the inner code, and both are independent of the chosen generator-row basis.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: The minimum helper-union size for an internally realizable rank-t demand equals the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight of the associated nested pair.
claims.objects: Relative weights and normalized linear target recovery systems.
claims.hypotheses: 1 <= t <= dim W_P; minimization ranges over all helper-recoverable t-dimensional target subspaces.
claims.conclusion: The minimum helper-union size for an internally realizable rank-t demand equals the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight of the associated nested pair.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: The relative dimension-length profile equals the maximum recoverable target-message dimension from a helper set of bounded size.
claims.objects: Relative dimension/length profile and dimensions recovered by helper subsets.
claims.hypotheses: The associated nested pair on the finite helper set; integer helper radius in the displayed domain.
claims.conclusion: The relative dimension-length profile equals the maximum recoverable target-message dimension from a helper set of bounded size.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: For a fixed nonzero target-message subspace, an outer code with at least two blocks, and a target block with nonzero outer projection, minimizing prescribed-coset union-support costs over linear maps into the complete outer functional dual gives the exact finite first nonconfined helper cost; minimizing over internally recoverable target subspaces gives the ranked criterion and exact transfer below it.
claims.objects: Linear maps into the outer functional dual and prescribed block lift costs.
claims.hypotheses: Represented inner encoder with nontrivial proper image; nonzero T; N>=2; distinguished outer projection surjective.
claims.conclusion: For a fixed nonzero target-message subspace, an outer code with at least two blocks, and a target block with nonzero outer projection, minimizing prescribed-coset union-support costs over linear maps into the complete outer functional dual gives the exact finite first nonconfined helper cost; minimizing over internally recoverable target subspaces gives the ranked criterion and exact transfer below it.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: Two extension-field representations of the same binary image code, with identical dual, target/helper nested pair, complete relative-weight hierarchy, dual distance, unlabelled normalized helper-support family, and zero-functional escape profile, have different exact nonconfinement costs for one fixed outer represented code because their costs align differently with the intermediate functional labels.
claims.objects: Two binary representations and a fixed F_4-linear outer dual line.
claims.hypotheses: The explicit encoders and trace pairing in the proof; target is the first coordinate.
claims.conclusion: Two extension-field representations of the same binary image code, with identical dual, target/helper nested pair, complete relative-weight hierarchy, dual distance, unlabelled normalized helper-support family, and zero-functional escape profile, have different exact nonconfinement costs for one fixed outer represented code because their costs align differently with the intermediate functional labels.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: Ordinary prescribed-coset union-support costs compose exactly by blockwise min-sum substitution under repeated concatenation and satisfy the stated sharp support envelopes; helper-restriction costs together with target images give the target-normalized recursion, and a compatible formula gives the composite dual distance and exact nonconfinement cost while keeping zero and nonzero functional sectors separate.
claims.objects: Ordinary and target-normalized label-indexed support costs through a field tower.
claims.hypotheses: Finite field tower with represented linear encoders; disjoint leaf blocks; all intermediate target images and functional labels retained.
claims.conclusion: Ordinary prescribed-coset union-support costs compose exactly by blockwise min-sum substitution under repeated concatenation and satisfy the stated sharp support envelopes; helper-restriction costs together with target images give the target-normalized recursion, and a compatible formula gives the composite dual distance and exact nonconfinement cost while keeping zero and nonzero functional sectors separate.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: Every compatible outer functional dual has a pointed coordinate-covector presentation whose external covectors span, and every such pointed spanning list realizes a compatible outer context up to change of functional-dual basis.
claims.objects: Pointed coordinate covectors representing an outer functional dual.
claims.hypotheses: An injective L-linear parametrization; compatibility means surjective distinguished outer projection, equivalently spanning external covectors.
claims.conclusion: Every compatible outer functional dual has a pointed coordinate-covector presentation whose external covectors span, and every such pointed spanning list realizes a compatible outer context up to change of functional-dual basis.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: For represented inner codes with an identified target/helper split and recoverable target line, the zero-functional escape cost and truncated projective line probes characterize exact numerical response equivalence over all finite outer contexts. Equality persists against composed outer contexts with the original leaf confinement region, target coordinates, and normalization fixed; no macroblock escape congruence is asserted.
claims.objects: Zero-sector cost and truncated projective line probes.
claims.hypotheses: Identified helper-recoverable target lines over the same extension field; N>=2 and nonzero distinguished projection; original leaf region fixed in composed-context evaluations.
claims.conclusion: For represented inner codes with an identified target/helper split and recoverable target line, the zero-functional escape cost and truncated projective line probes characterize exact numerical response equivalence over all finite outer contexts. Equality persists against composed outer contexts with the original leaf confinement region, target coordinates, and normalization fixed; no macroblock escape congruence is asserted.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement. Numerical equivalence observes escape from the original leaf; it does not preserve new macroblock observations, support alternatives, or arbitrary prices.

claims.statement: For a nonzero rank-t target, exact nonconfinement cost is the minimum over functional-dual subcontexts of dimension at most t; through helper radius r it is determined by contexts of length at most max(2,r+1) and functional-dual dimension at most min(t,r), every unequal bounded response has a separator within those bounds, and every bounded coefficient-level witness restricts to and zero-extends from such a context.
claims.objects: Rank-bounded dual subcontexts, bounded separators, and coefficient witnesses.
claims.hypotheses: Finite base and extension fields, nonzero helper-recoverable rank-t target, integer r>=0, represented encoders and compatible outer contexts.
claims.conclusion: For a nonzero rank-t target, exact nonconfinement cost is the minimum over functional-dual subcontexts of dimension at most t; through helper radius r it is determined by contexts of length at most max(2,r+1) and functional-dual dimension at most min(t,r), every unequal bounded response has a separator within those bounds, and every bounded coefficient-level witness restricts to and zero-extends from such a context.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: For each finite field, nonzero rank-t target, and helper radius r, the finite bounded-context response vector is the coarsest exact bounded numerical equivalence. Equality persists against composed outer contexts with the original leaf confinement region and target normalization fixed. For helper-recoverable targets the zero-sector value gives an exact finite untruncated test bound.
claims.objects: Finite truncated response vector and untruncated zero-sector bound.
claims.hypotheses: Same finite fields, identified nonzero target normalization, nontrivial proper inner code; original leaf boundary fixed; finite zero-sector bound for helper-recoverable targets.
claims.conclusion: For each finite field, nonzero rank-t target, and helper radius r, the finite bounded-context response vector is the coarsest exact bounded numerical equivalence. Equality persists against composed outer contexts with the original leaf confinement region and target normalization fixed. For helper-recoverable targets the zero-sector value gives an exact finite untruncated test bound.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement. Numerical equivalence observes escape from the original leaf; it does not preserve new macroblock observations, support alternatives, or arbitrary prices.

claims.statement: For a fixed target/helper split and target block with nonzero outer projection, rank-one confinement through a radius is equivalent to simultaneous confinement at every recoverable rank; below the gate restriction and zero-extension preserve every bounded coefficient-labelled system, exact support, bounded reliability law, support-determined scheduling region, and truncated minimum-union cost.
claims.objects: Simultaneous confinement and exact bounded coefficient/support data.
claims.hypotheses: A fixed target split with nonzero recoverable targets, surjective distinguished projection, and a nonnegative integer helper radius.
claims.conclusion: For a fixed target/helper split and target block with nonzero outer projection, rank-one confinement through a radius is equivalent to simultaneous confinement at every recoverable rank; below the gate restriction and zero-extension preserve every bounded coefficient-labelled system, exact support, bounded reliability law, support-determined scheduling region, and truncated minimum-union cost.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: A min-sum dynamic program over intermediate labels computes exact prescribed-coset support costs and returns one coefficient-level witness per finite entry when local lifts are supplied. The O(NQ) predecessor bound retains one minimizer per entry; all tied transitions and expanded recoveries have separate storage and output costs.
claims.objects: Finite functional-label DP with local support-cost tables.
claims.hypotheses: Enumerated finite label spaces, additive costs on disjoint blocks; one selected predecessor per finite entry and supplied local lifts for coefficient reconstruction.
claims.conclusion: A min-sum dynamic program over intermediate labels computes exact prescribed-coset support costs and returns one coefficient-level witness per finite entry when local lifts are supplied. The O(NQ) predecessor bound retains one minimizer per entry; all tied transitions and expanded recoveries have separate storage and output costs.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement.

claims.statement: For a nonzero internally realizable target subspace, under d(O^perp)>r+1 and N>=2, every radius-r normalized system is confined exactly when r is below the local target cost plus inner dual distance; dual-distance growth gives the eventual family form.
claims.objects: Fixed-target coefficient confinement and support-preserving bijection.
claims.hypotheses: 0 != T <= W_P, N>=2, and d(O^perp)>r+1 for a nonnegative integer r.
claims.conclusion: For a nonzero internally realizable target subspace, under d(O^perp)>r+1 and N>=2, every radius-r normalized system is confined exactly when r is below the local target cost plus inner dual distance; dual-distance growth gives the eventual family form.

claims.statement: Under the finite outer gate, the uniform rank-t nonconfinement helper threshold is the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight plus the inner dual distance; the same holds eventually in outer families of growing dual distance.
claims.objects: Uniform rank-t coefficient confinement and relative helper weights.
claims.hypotheses: 1 <= t <= dim W_P, N>=2, and the stated finite outer-distance gate; minimization is over all recoverable rank-t targets.
claims.conclusion: Under the finite outer gate, the uniform rank-t nonconfinement helper threshold is the t-th relative generalized Hamming weight plus the inner dual distance; the same holds eventually in outer families of growing dual distance.

claims.statement: For one target coordinate and any finite outer code with nonzero target-block projection, target-constrained inner coset weights give the exact minimum total weight of a nonconfined concatenated dual word and hence an ungated if-and-only-if transfer criterion at every helper radius.
claims.objects: Total-weight cost of a target-normalized nonconfined dual word.
claims.hypotheses: Represented inner code, one specified target coordinate, N>=2 and nonzero distinguished outer projection; empty minima have value infinity.

claims.statement: A construction using a Singer cycle and [k+1,k,2]_q inner codes, with k+1 <= n <= 2k+1, satisfies the exact weighted nonvacuous radius-(n-1) transfer gate although the ordinary outer support-distance gate fails; the [4,3,2]_5, n=5 case is explicit.
claims.objects: Single-parity-check inner code and multiplier-aligned outer parity code.
claims.hypotheses: k>=2, (q^k-1)/(q-1)>(k+1)^2, and k+1<=n<=2k+1; helper radius n-1.
claims.conclusion: A construction using a Singer cycle and [k+1,k,2]_q inner codes, with k+1 <= n <= 2k+1, satisfies the exact weighted nonvacuous radius-(n-1) transfer gate although the ordinary outer support-distance gate fails; the [4,3,2]_5, n=5 case is explicit.

claims.statement: The minimum simultaneous helper cost over target e-sets is d_e(C^perp)-e. For N>=2 and represented inner code C, outer dual distance at least d_e(C^perp)-e+d(C^perp)+1 forces the minimum nonconfined identity-system cost over these sets to equal d_e(C^perp)-e+d(C^perp); nonzero-sector ties are allowed.
claims.objects: Coordinate identity recovery, generalized dual weights, and minimum escape over target e-sets.
claims.hypotheses: 1<=e<=dim C^perp; for escape use represented C, N>=2, and d(O^perp)>=d_e(C^perp)-e+d(C^perp)+1.
claims.conclusion: The minimum simultaneous helper cost over target e-sets is d_e(C^perp)-e. For N>=2 and represented inner code C, outer dual distance at least d_e(C^perp)-e+d(C^perp)+1 forces the minimum nonconfined identity-system cost over these sets to equal d_e(C^perp)-e+d(C^perp); nonzero-sector ties are allowed.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement. The finite bound controls a minimum over target sets and allows nonzero-sector ties.

claims.statement: Growing outer dual distance eventually preserves minimal supports at every fixed radius on every block; the additional inner bounds remain necessary for the stated coefficient-transfer specialization. Global rate and distance bounds are unchanged.

claims.statement: For a fixed query and supplied binary tree of finite linear factors, each feasible boundary is an affine space of q^(t w_S) syndromes. Scalar optimization costs O(n q^(2tw)) pair combinations plus local table scans and linear algebra, with an additional (r+1)^2 factor for a separate support budget.
claims.objects: Affine cut contribution spaces and scalar optimization on a supplied binary tree.
claims.hypotheses: Fixed linear query of rank parameter t; finite local tables on disjoint physical blocks; local compilation and polynomial arithmetic charged separately.
claims.conclusion: For a fixed query and supplied binary tree of finite linear factors, each feasible boundary is an affine space of q^(t w_S) syndromes. Scalar optimization costs O(n q^(2tw)) pair combinations plus local table scans and linear algebra, with an additional (r+1)^2 factor for a separate support budget.
claims.cautions: Human proof only; no Lean terminal or computational evidence is asserted for this statement. Counts state-pair combinations, not total bit complexity or the construction cost of unspecified local interfaces.
